property.value:
### Exposing elements as Azure Functions (`Azure Function` stereotype) - Apply the `Azure Function` stereotype to an `Operation`, `Command` or `Query` to expose it as an Azure Function (one function class per element). A standalone `Azure Function` element (`New Azure Function` on a Services Package or Folder) gets the stereotype automatically when created. - Operations are generated only when Intent.AzureFunctions.Dispatch.Services is installed, and Commands/Queries only when Intent.AzureFunctions.Dispatch.MediatR is installed. Without them the stereotype on those elements produces nothing. - Set `Trigger` first. It decides which other properties are shown and required. Leave hidden properties unset; `Route`, `Method` and `Return Type Mediatype` are legacy, always hidden, and never set. - The stereotype applies once per element, so each element has exactly one trigger. To run the same logic from two triggers, model two elements.
### Trigger properties - `Http Trigger` (default): set `Authorization Level` (default `Function`; use `Anonymous` only for public endpoints). The verb and route come from the WebApi `Http Settings` stereotype, not from this one. The designer adds `Http Settings` with a conventional verb and route when the trigger is Http; confirm it is present and correct `Verb`/`Route` (and parameter sources) there. Switching to any other trigger removes `Http Settings`. - An Azure Function's `Http Settings` Route must NOT start with `api/`: the Functions host already prefixes routes with `api` (`host.json` `extensions.http.routePrefix`). Write `orders/{id}`, not `api/orders/{id}`, otherwise the endpoint becomes `/api/api/orders/{id}`. This overrides any designer rule asking for a fully qualified route. - `Service Bus Trigger`: `Queue Name` is optional; blank uses the payload type name. Set `Subscription Name` to consume a topic subscription, in which case `Queue Name` is the topic name. Leave `Subscription Name` blank for a queue. - `Queue Trigger` (Azure Storage Queue): `Queue Name` is required. `Include Message Envelope` binds the raw `QueueMessage` instead of the deserialized payload. When the element has a return type, a `Queue Output Binding` stereotype is added; set its `Queue Name` to the queue the result is written to. - `Timer Trigger`: `Schedule Expression` is required and is a six-field NCRONTAB expression, e.g. `0 */5 * * * *` (every 5 minutes). Parameters are ignored. - `EventHub Trigger`: `EventHub Name` is required. - `RabbitMQ Trigger`: `Queue Name` is required. - `Cosmos DB Trigger`: a separate `Cosmos DB Trigger` stereotype is added; fill its `Connection`, `Database Name`, `Container Name` and `Lease Container Name` (all required). The payload is generated as `IReadOnlyCollection<T>` of the parameter's type. - `Manual Trigger`: no further properties. - `Connection` (where shown) is the NAME of an app setting holding the connection string, never the connection string itself. Never put secrets in the model.
### Payload rules for non-HTTP triggers - On a `Command` or `Query`, the Command/Query itself is the message payload; do not add anything else. - On an `Operation` or `Azure Function` element, model EXACTLY ONE parameter, typed as the message payload (Timer excepted). Zero or more than one parameter fails the Software Factory run.
### App settings - Trigger names (queue, topic, subscription, event hub, Cosmos DB database/container, schedule) are written literally by default; a value may be entered as `%SettingKey%` to resolve from configuration. When the `Trigger Names From App Settings` module setting is enabled, they are emitted as `%AzureFunctions:{FunctionName}:{Part}%` and seeded into `local.settings.json` automatically, so enter plain values, not `%...%`.
### Anti-patterns - Using a Service Bus-triggered Azure Function to consume an Eventing-designer integration event or command. Model a subscription in the Eventing/Services designers instead (handled by Intent.AzureFunctions.AzureServiceBus). - Setting verb/route on the `Azure Function` stereotype instead of `Http Settings`. - Adding extra parameters to a non-HTTP Operation or `Azure Function` element.
